annotations.annotation_text: ALP invocation "washerwomen" on page 183 ("Shem the Penman"): Anna Livia Plurabelle, the mother-river personifying the Liffey, surfaces here amid Joyce's devastating self-portrait as Shem the forger-artist who writes on his own skin with bodily secretions. In this Age of Gods passage, her feminine current of forgiveness and renewal flows through the dream landscape, carrying Dublin's history from source to sea.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Hart, Clive. Structure and Motif in Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/structuremotifin0000hart
Mink, Louis O. A Finnegans Wake Gazetteer. https://archive.org/details/finneganswakegaz0000mink
FWEET: ALP / River Liffey concordance. https://www.fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "broken" on page 183 ("Shem the Penman"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within Joyce's devastating self-portrait as Shem the forger-artist who writes on his own skin with bodily secretions. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Age of Gods phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Opie, Iona and Peter. The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes. https://archive.org/details/oxforddictionary0000unse_m4u1
